expected_findings.reason: retry_many() assigns each task a fresh task_id via uuid4 instead of reusing the original, breaking downstream dedupe on task_id -- the same violation as pr-03, but here it's the only defect in a 3-file, 30-line diff that also adds two unrelated, correct helpers (count_pending, __init__ re-exports) and ships with a docstring that argues for the violation as an intentional design choice ('to avoid id collisions'). Built to test whether a role fanning out narrows in on this specific defect any more reliably than a generalist reading the whole diff at once (docs/roadmap.md M3 stop condition) -- the M0-sized corpus's single-defect, single-file diffs couldn't test this.

note: Result (2026-09-14): no differentiation on the intended axis -- the generalist and the 3-role fan-out both caught the INV-3 violation cleanly (correctness AND convention independently, from different angles), so 'buried in noise' wasn't actually hard for a frontier single-pass model. Real bonus finding though: the simplification role independently caught that retry_many() duplicates the FAILED->PENDING transition inline instead of calling retry() -- a genuine defect in this fixture's own code, unintentional, unanticipated by this file, and missed by the generalist and by the other two roles. That's real marginal contribution, just not on the axis this fixture was designed to test, and it's invisible to harness/backtest.py's scoring (score() only checks expected_findings above -- there's no way for a correct finding outside that list to register as anything other than silently ignored). See docs/roadmap.md M3, 2026-09-14 entry.
